title: Packaging a pack without breaking anyone's install
hook: All packs share one Python. One careless pin moves a library under every other pack. Here is the layout, the pyproject, and how to stay out of trouble.

verified.claim: A core node name can't be replaced by a pack. Between two packs, the later one wins with no message, and the order comes from os.listdir.
An exception during import is logged as a warning, the pack is marked IMPORT FAILED, and other packs carry on.
ComfyUI does not install a pack's requirements when it loads it.
verified.ref: main.py and nodes.py have no such step; the only pip text in main.py is a message about the manager's own requirements

verified.claim: prestartup_script.py in a pack runs before the rest of startup.
example_workflows is served as templates. Four other names are served too, with a debug-level line suggesting a rename, and any other name isn't served.
pyproject fields: name, version, PublisherId and the name rules.
pip's --dry-run prints what would be installed, and -c applies a constraints file.

unchecked: We didn't publish a pack or run the registry's checks for this lesson.
We didn't run pip here. The advice on dry runs comes from pip's docs, and the lab's version check is a teaching model of one idea, not a resolver.
The docs we fetched don't say how a pack manager installs dependencies, so we say nothing about what a given manager does.
